describes: The finishing test's materials and marks: each material's lightness (CIE L*) and gloss in clay, its tileable, and how strongly each mark reads from 107's facts. marks.py and tiles.py read it; the Unity scene reads the materials. Values are the look's, tuned by looking; the rules that use them are in the scripts.

scans.describes: Ways B and C's tileables, from the CC0 scans in blender/parts/finish/scans/ (logged in docs/research/downloads.md). Each scan is remapped about its material's lightness at `contrast` times its own spread, its gloss at `glossContrast` times its own, and nothing finer than `killMm` survives. `metres` is the scan's real size. Planks: the plank faces between the scan's seams, stacked across v so no seam of the scan lands on one of ours.

tiles.describes: Way A's tileables (tiles.py): each surface's own structure, in metres of the 2 m tile, L* about the material's lightness and relief in mm. Nothing here is history; the page carries that.

marks.describes: Marks read 107's facts: the house's age, its neglect (per mille, the engine's) and the years since it was boarded, and the sample's geometry and features. Lightness shifts are in L*; sizes in metres. Loss groups: `length` and `height` are ranges the seed draws in, `strength` the share of the group's paint lost at its heart.

painted.describes: Way P (paint.py; the shader's _OS_PAINT): the corner painted as a painter would, in a few broad designed value shapes from 107's facts, by the value plan in reviews/lt1/finish/p1. Each material is one value (albedo L*), shifted by three unequal planes (the wall's one gradient, the window dark, the sun's shadow) and by one failed-paint shape that follows the water, its wash and its peel two marks told apart by value and edge (the paint, then the soft wash, then the bare fibre, hard-edged and darkest, its torn edge lipped with paint film that catches the sun). Each course takes its own tone; far, the laps collapse to a few broad strokes. The failed paint's strength follows the house's wear (`wear`: 1 at 107, neglect 600 and boarded 3 years; a guess until a second house is judged). A material's `ao` and `contact` say how much of the geometry's occlusion it keeps, and `shadowLift` (m) how far toward the light it looks for its shadow, so its own small forms cast none: the roof, painted as one mass, keeps little and casts none on itself. Way P has its own overcast, a soft sky from the street that parts the gable from the street wall. Sizes in metres, values in L*.

colour.describes: The colour still (Øystein, 28 October: one in p2, the one exception to clay-first): only hue and chroma, laid on the clay's own L*, so the clay and colour stills share their values. Each colour is [C, h], CIE LCh: a material's at its own clay L* (its paint, bare fibre, under layer and stain at their values; the wash at the paint's less `tongue.washL`), turned to a tint of luminance 1, so its albedo keeps the clay's luminance; a light's as it reads alone on a neutral white at `atL`, its strength the clay's; the plain sky behind (`background`) at its clay L*, the third number, and the ground (`floor`) at `ground.L`. Muted all over; true colour only where people keep things, and 107 is not kept. Shade and ambient take the light's colour, never the object's (VD2).

boarding.describes: The boarded window: a, the sheet dark as in look 1; b, a weathered mid-grey sheet whose stain is the dark accent, the battens lighter so they cross it (kept after the A/B at the street stop); c, the battens raw-sawn and weathered grey on a dark sheet, so the window is the wall's dark shape. The sheet's damp runs down from its head to a slow tide line (`tide`). `use` is the one kept.

lip.describes: The torn edge's lip: the paint film lifted along it, curling over the bare fibre, `widthMm` wide, the paint's own value lighter by `L`, turned to the light by `face` and lit only by the key light, as strongly as that light is directional; in pieces about `cell` long over `share` of the edge.

wear.describes: How far the paint has failed, from the house's facts: (neglect / `neglect` x (years since neglect + `lead`) / (`years` + `lead`)) ^ `power`, 1 at 107; the tongue's values and sizes scale by it.

ply.describes: The sheet reads as ply: its face veneer's long wavy figure along each sheet's long side (`figure`, [across, along] cells, its lines wandering by `wave`); `each` oval patches a sheet where the mill cut out knots; its cut edges drinking, darkest along the foot (`edge`); a nail every `spacing` round its edge, `insetMm` in.

far.describes: Far off, the laps collapse into the wall's plane but for a few kept ones (paint.py lap_keep: on the street wall the butts at the drip, the sill and the head; on the gable, `plain` shares of its height), drawn broader by `reach`: from `mmPerPx[0]` a pixel, gone by `mmPerPx[1]`.

wall.describes: The wall's one gradient, `topL` under the eave to `footL` at the drip board (by the house's wear), eased by `power`; each course takes the gradient's value at its middle (`course`) and its own small step (`courseJitter`), kept apart (page 2's A, within `toneRange`) with each butt's own thin line of contact shade (`contact.lapPx`), so far off they go with the laps.

plinth.describes: Darker toward the ground (`L`), each block its own small step (`blockL`); its top, under the drip board's overhang, takes little sky (`capL`).

junction.describes: The dark where one thing meets another: at the junction the value is drawn down to `to` (L*), easing back over `reach`.

tongue.describes: The one failed-paint shape, following the water: off the sill's ends (the leaking one most) to the plinth, and down beside the casing from the head's leaking end. Its wash is soft and darker than the paint, water and dirt: on each board it spreads toward the drip edge, where the water lingers, and the board below takes it narrower again. Its peel is bare silvered fibre, darker still and hard-edged, keeping only `bareWash` of the wash: a few long thin slivers along the grain (`slivers.sizes`, [length, height], largest first), each creeping up from a board's drip edge, tallest at the run's core and tapering out to ragged ends. The largest goes where the water stays longest (the run's strength, more at a butt joint under it and low down), one to a course. Each board's share of both is its own, so no mark crosses a lap. Sizes and strengths are 107's, scaled by the house's wear.

batten.describes: Raw-sawn battens, weathered grey: a faint grain of streaks along them (`grain`, [along, across] cells); their sawn ends lifted by `endL` to the batten's own grey, so no end reads as a dark peg.

wet.describes: The plinth's foot kept damp by splash, a soft dark (`L`) up to `top`, higher by `splash` under the drips that carry most, its edge `soft` either side: no found line.
